instructions: This is hermes-hunt-bots, a fork of NousResearch/hermes-agent that adds a human-gated six-bot threat-hunting framework under framework/. Review every PR against HUNT-BOTS.md (project rules, which override upstream guidance) and framework/AGENTS.md. Flag as blocking: real or non-synthetic data, credentials or tokens, anything marked CUI/NSS, bot tools that can write, control the VM, reach non-lab hosts or read answer keys, browser automation that can open non-lab origins, fabricated approvals/evidence/scores, weakened guards or tests, docs claiming 'enforced' without a runtime test, copied third-party code without its license notice and a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md entry, and new framework/ files missing from framework/TRACKED-FILES.txt.

rules.rule: Bot lab tools must stay read-only, scoped to the loaded case, and reach only the guest lab service on 127.0.0.1; never add VM control, live capture, other hosts, or answer-key access.
Refusals relay only fixed snake_case error codes to the bot, never backend free text; keep host advertised field lists equal to the guest allowlists (test_hunt_lab_tools.py).
Workflow behavior changes must be gated by a new workflow.patched() ID so recorded histories replay unchanged, keep human execute/review gates, and never add retries without explicit approval.
Operator-only material (answer keys, truth.json, scoring rubrics) must never be reachable from bot prompts, tools, or the guest payload.
Browser automation must enforce a lab-origin allowlist inside the browser (navigations, frames, new tabs), not only by scanning code for URLs.

Every tracked framework/ file must be listed in framework/TRACKED-FILES.txt; the portable package allowlist (framework/package_portable.py FILES and test_package_portable.py APPROVED_FILES) must stay in sync for shipped files.

files.description: Project rules for the fork; they override upstream guidance.
Framework behavior, safety boundaries and verification evidence.
